name: Character Studio
intro: Character Studio keeps one face consistent. Add a clear reference photo and a description, and get the same person in a new outfit, scene or mood.

features.model-selector-flux-pulid-subject-refere: The model selector at the top offers two face-preserving models. Try Flux PuLID first to keep a face recognisable, or Subject Reference for a different look.
features.reference-face: Reference Face is the most important input. Upload a clear face photo or video, or browse stock photos from Pexels, and the model copies the identity from it.
features.character-description: Character Description is where you describe clothes, place, lighting and mood. Leave the face to your reference, so only the scene changes between images.
features.expression-presets: Expression Presets give you Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised and Neutral. Click one and matching words are added to your description for you.
features.advanced-panel: The Advanced button reveals extra options for the model you chose, such as aspect ratio, when that model offers them.
features.three-dot-tools-menu: The three-dot menu holds GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize and Prompts, which help you write prompts or find ideas for your character content.
features.saved-characters: Saved Characters lists characters stored in your browser. Click one to load its image and description straight back into the form.

outro: That's Character Studio. Start with a sharp reference, describe a new scene, and change one thing at a time to see what works best.
